title: What is Automatic Speech Recognition? A Comprehensive Overview of ASR Technology
summary: This article aims to answer the question: What is ASR?, and provide a comprehensive overview of Automatic Speech Recognition technology.
body_text: Automatic Speech Recognition, also known as ASR, is the use of AI technology to process human speech into readable text. The field has grown exponentially over the past decade, and market projections show it's expected to reach a market volume of US$73 billion by 2031. ASR systems now power applications we use every day—from TikTok and Instagram's real-time captions to Spotify's podcast transcriptions and Zoom's meeting notes. As ASR approaches human accuracy levels, we're seeing an explosion of applications taking advantage of this technology to make audio and video data more accessible. Speech-to-text APIs like AssemblyAI are making ASR technology more affordable, accessible, and accurate for developers and businesses of all sizes. This comprehensive guide covers the fundamentals of Automatic Speech Recognition technology. You'll learn what ASR is and how it evolved, understand the technical approaches that power modern systems, and discover how businesses are using this technology today. We'll also explore current challenges and what's coming next in the field of speech recognition. What is Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)? A Brief History Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is AI technology that converts spoken language into written text by analyzing audio waveforms and identifying patterns in human speech. Modern ASR systems can transcribe conversations in real-time with accuracy approaching human-level performance. Early research confirms ASR extends back to 1952 when Bell Labs created "Audrey," a digit recognizer that could identify spoken numbers, though it required users to pause after each digit. Audrey could only transcribe spoken numbers, but a decade later, researchers improved upon the system so it could transcribe rudimentary spoken words like "hello." For most of the past fifteen years, ASR was powered by classical machine learning technologies like Hidden Markov Models. Though once the industry standard, accuracy of these classical models had plateaued in recent years. This plateau opened the door for advanced AI technology that's also powered breakthroughs in self-driving cars. In 2014, Baidu published the landmark paper, Deep Speech: Scaling up end-to-end speech recognition . The paper's published results , which achieved a 16% error rate on a standard benchmark, demonstrated AI's power in speech recognition and kicked off a renaissance in ASR. This AI-powered approach pushed model accuracy past the plateau and closer to human-level performance. Not only has accuracy skyrocketed, but access to ASR technology has also improved dramatically. Ten years ago, customers would have to engage in lengthy, expensive enterprise speech recognition software contracts to license ASR technology. Today, developers, startup companies, and Fortune 500s have access to advanced ASR technology via simple APIs like AssemblyAI's speech-to-text API . Test Speech-to-Text in Your Browser Upload audio or video and see accurate transcripts in seconds—no code required. Explore ASR capabilities hands-on before integrating the API. Try it here Let's look more closely at the two dominant approaches to ASR and understand how they work. How ASR Works Today, there are two main approaches to Automatic Speech Recognition: Traditional Hybrid Approach : Uses separate lexicon, acoustic, and language models working together ‍ End-to-End AI Approach: Employs a single unified model that directly maps audio to text Understanding these differences helps explain why modern ASR systems achieve such impressive accuracy. Traditional Hybrid Approach The traditional hybrid approach is the legacy approach to speech recognition and dominated the field for the past fifteen years. Many companies still rely on this approach simply because it's the way it has always been done—there's extensive research and training data available, despite plateaus in accuracy. Here's how the traditional approach works: Traditional HMM and GMM Systems Traditional HMM (Hidden Markov Models) and GMM (Gaussian Mixture Models) require forced aligned data. Force alignment determines where in time particular words occur in an audio segment. This approach combines three separate models: Lexicon Model: Describes phonetic pronunciation of words Acoustic Model: Predicts phonemes from audio segments Language Model: Predicts word sequences and probabilities Lexicon Model The lexicon model describes how words are pronounced phonetically. You need a custom phoneme set for each language, handcrafted by expert phoneticians. Acoustic Model The acoustic model (AM) models the acoustic patterns of speech. The job of the acoustic model is to predict which sound or phoneme is being spoken at each speech segment from the forced aligned data. The acoustic model is usually of an HMM or GMM variant. Language Model The language model (LM) models the statistics of language. It learns which sequences of words are most likely to be spoken, and its job is to predict which words will follow on from the current words and with what probability. Decoding Decoding is a process of utilizing the lexicon, acoustic, and language models to produce a transcript. Downsides of the Traditional Approach Though still widely used, the traditional hybrid approach to speech recognition has several drawbacks. Lower accuracy is the biggest challenge. Each model must be trained independently, making them time and labor intensive. Forced aligned data is difficult to come by and requires significant human labor. Experts are needed to build custom phonetic sets to boost the model's accuracy. End-to-End AI Approach An end-to-end AI approach represents a newer way of thinking about ASR, and how we approach ASR here at AssemblyAI. How End-to-End AI Models Work With an end-to-end system, you can directly map a sequence of input acoustic features into a sequence of words. The data doesn't need to be force-aligned. Depending on the architecture, an AI system can be trained to produce accurate transcripts without a lexicon model and language model, although language models can help produce more accurate results. Modern Architectures: CTC, LAS, and RNNTs CTC, LAS, and RNNTs are popular speech recognition end-to-end AI architectures. These systems can be trained to produce highly accurate results without needing force aligned data, lexicon models, and language models. Advantages of End-to-End AI Models End-to-end AI models are easier to train and require less human labor than a traditional approach. They're also more accurate than the traditional models being used today. The AI research community is actively searching for ways to constantly improve these models using the latest research. There's no concern of accuracy plateaus any time soon—in fact, we'll see AI models reach human level accuracy in the next few years. Build with Accurate ASR APIs Leverage end-to-end AI models for reliable transcription across diverse audio. Create a free account and start transcribing in minutes. Start free Comparing Traditional vs. Modern ASR Approaches Aspect Traditional Hybrid End-to-End AI Components Lexicon + Acoustic + Language Models Single unified model Training Data Requires force-aligned data Works with unaligned audio-text pairs Human Labor High (phoneticians, alignment) Minimal Accuracy Trend Plateaued Continuously improving Setup Complexity High (multiple models) Lower (single system) Customization Requires expert knowledge Can be fine-tuned with data ASR Accuracy and Performance Metrics Not all ASR systems are created equal. The quality of transcription can make or break user experience. Word Error Rate (WER) is the industry standard for measuring ASR accuracy. It compares machine-generated transcripts to human-verified transcripts and calculates error percentage. The formula is simple: WER = (Substitutions + Deletions + Insertions) / Number of Words in Reference Transcript A lower WER means higher accuracy. For example, a WER of 10% means that 90% of the words were transcribed correctly. However, WER doesn't tell the whole story. Real-world audio presents multiple challenges: Background noise and poor audio quality Overlapping speakers and interruptions Unique accents and speaking styles Industry-specific jargon and terminology This is why one ASR system might feel seamless while another feels clumsy. Modern AI models, like AssemblyAI's Universal models, are trained on millions of hours of diverse audio data to perform reliably across these challenging conditions. ASR Key Terms and Features Acoustic Model: The acoustic model takes in audio waveforms and predicts what words are present in the waveform. Language Model : The language model can be used to help guide and correct the acoustic model's predictions. Word Error Rate : The industry standard measurement of how accurate an ASR transcription is, as compared to a human transcription. Speaker Diarization : Answers the question, who spoke when? Also referred to as speaker labels. Custom Vocabulary : Custom vocabulary boosts accuracy for a list of specific keywords or phrases when transcribing an audio file. Sentiment Analysis : The sentiment, typically positive, negative, or neutral, of specific speech segments in an audio or video file. See more models specific to AssemblyAI . Key Applications of ASR Modern ASR delivers measurable value across diverse industries. Key applications include: Telephony: Call tracking , cloud phone solutions, and contact centers need accurate transcriptions, as well as innovative analytical features like Conversation Intelligence , call analytics, speaker diarization, and more. Video Platforms: Real-time and asynchronous video captioning are industry standard. Video editing platforms (and video editors alike) also need content categorization and content moderation to improve accessibility and search. Media Monitoring : Speech-to-text APIs can help broadcast TV, podcasts, radio, and more quickly and accurately detect brand and other topic mentions for better advertising. Virtual Meetings : Meeting platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, WebEx, and more need accurate transcriptions and the ability to analyze this content to drive key insights and action. Choosing a Speech-to-Text API With more APIs on the market, how do you know which speech-to-text API is best for your application ? When considering which API to use, one insights report found that the top factors for buyers are cost, quality, accuracy, and ease of use. Key considerations to keep in mind include: How accurate the API is What additional models are offered What kind of support you can expect Pricing and documentation transparency Data security Company innovation Companies like Aloware use highly accurate ASR to power smart transcription and speed up QA for their customers. CallRail doubled its Conversational Intelligence customers by integrating AI-powered ASR into its platform and building powerful Generative AI products on top of the transcription data. Marvin added AI transcription to build a suite of AI-powered tools and features that resulted in significantly less time analyzing research data for its customers. Challenges of ASR Today One of the main challenges of ASR today is the continual push toward human accuracy levels. While both ASR approaches—traditional hybrid and end-to-end AI—are significantly more accurate than ever before, neither can claim 100% human accuracy. There's so much nuance in the way we speak, from dialects to slang to pitch. Even the best AI models can't be trained to cover this long tail of edge cases without significant effort. Some think they can solve this accuracy problem with custom speech-to-text models . However, unless you have a very specific use case, like children's speech, custom models are actually less accurate, harder to train, and more expensive in practice than a good end-to-end AI model. Another top concern is speech-to-text privacy for APIs . In fact, a recent industry survey found that over 30% of respondents cited data privacy as a significant challenge, as many large ASR companies use customer data to train models without explicit permission. Continual data storage in the cloud also raises concerns over potential security breaches, especially if raw audio or video files or transcription text contains Personally Identifiable Information. On the Horizon for ASR As the field of ASR continues to grow, we can expect to see greater integration of speech-to-text technology into our everyday lives, as well as more widespread industry applications. We're already seeing advancements in ASR and related AI fields taking place at an accelerated rate. Examples include OpenAI's ChatGPT, HuggingFace spaces and AI applications , and AssemblyAI's Universal model . In regards to model building, we also expect to see a shift to a self-supervised learning system to solve some of the challenges with accuracy discussed above. End-to-end AI models are data hungry. Our Universal model at AssemblyAI, for example, is trained on millions of hours of raw audio and video training data for industry-best accuracy levels. However, obtaining human transcriptions for this same training data would be almost impossible given the time constraints associated with human processing speeds. This is where self-supervised AI systems can help. Essentially, this is a way to get an abundance of unlabeled data and build a foundational model on top of it. Then, since we have statistical knowledge of the data, we can fine-tune it on downstream tasks with a smaller amount of data, making it a more accessible approach to model building. This is an exciting possibility with profound implications for the field. If this transition occurs, expect ASR models to become even more accurate and affordable, making their use and acceptance more widespread. Ready to experience the power of modern ASR technology? Try our API for free and see how accurate speech recognition can transform your applications. Frequently Asked Questions About Automatic Speech Recognition What is the difference between ASR and NLP? ASR converts spoken audio into written text, while NLP analyzes that text to understand meaning, intent, and sentiment. Think of ASR as the ears and NLP as the brain—they work together in Voice AI applications. Is ASR the same as speech-to-text? Yes, ASR and speech-to-text are used interchangeably. ASR is the underlying technology, while speech-to-text describes the function it performs. What is the difference between speech recognition and voice recognition? Speech recognition transcribes what is being said, while voice recognition identifies who is speaking by matching unique voiceprints. Speech recognition creates transcripts; voice recognition labels speakers. Is ASR a form of AI? Yes, modern ASR uses AI models to convert human speech into text. The most advanced ASR systems use sophisticated AI architectures that continuously learn and improve from vast amounts of audio data. How accurate is modern ASR compared to humans? Modern ASR systems achieve Word Error Rates below 5% on clear audio, approaching human-level accuracy in ideal conditions. Performance varies with background noise, accents, and overlapping speakers, where humans still maintain advantages in contextual understanding. ‍

title: Days Sales Outstanding Benchmarks for Dental Practices in 2026
body_text: Days sales outstanding benchmarks for dental practices: under 25 days is excellent, 25–30 days is good, 30–45 days is the industry average, and over 45 days signals a revenue cycle breakdown requiring immediate action. Solo practices typically run 40–60 days DSO; top-performing DSO organizations with centralized billing consistently hit under 25 days. Group practices with standardized billing workflows typically land at 30–45 days. This guide covers the complete DSO benchmarks by practice type, the AR aging targets that underpin them, and seven proven strategies to reduce your dental days in AR to top-quartile performance. Production is up, the schedule is full, but cash is tight that's the signature of a high-DSO practice. DSO measures how long it takes to collect payment after delivering a service, and most practices carry far more locked-up revenue in unpaid claims and patient balances than they realize. Most dental practices average 30–45 days DSO industry best practice is under 30 days, and top-performing DSO organizations consistently hit under 25. Insurance denial rates climbed from 11% (2022) to 15% (2026) , meaning practices are fighting harder to collect revenue they've already earned. The fastest DSO gains come upstream: 48-hour insurance pre-verification, same-day claim submission, and capturing every inbound call before a scheduling error becomes a billing failure. Key Takeaways Benchmark the right range: Most dental practices average 30–45 days DSO industry best practice is under 30 days, and top-performing DSO organizations consistently hit under 25 days. Aging AR is largely unrecoverable: Only 15–25% of balances past 90 days are typically collected, making early intervention critical to your cash flow. Denial rates are rising: Insurance denial rates in dentistry climbed from roughly 11% in 2022 to approximately 15% in 2024–2026, directly inflating dental days in AR across the industry. Patient balances are under-collected: The industry average patient collection rate runs 70–80% the target is 90%+, leaving thousands in uncollected revenue per month. Practice type matters: Solo practices typically run 40–60 days DSO; group practices 30–45 days; top-performing DSO organizations hit under 25 days with centralized billing. 85%+ of your AR belongs in the 0–30 day bucket: Anything less signals a revenue cycle breakdown that will compound over time. Upstream actions protect DSO: Capturing insurance data before the appointment and answering every inbound call are two of the highest-leverage actions for keeping the billing cycle clean from day one. AI receptionists sound human and collect billing data: Modern AI receptionists for dental practices handle scheduling calls naturally patients rarely know they're speaking with AI and collect insurance carrier, member ID, and date of birth during the call so billing starts with clean, verified data. What Is Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) in Dentistry? Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) measures the average number of days between delivering a dental service and receiving payment capturing how efficiently your revenue cycle converts production into cash. In dental billing, "days in AR" and "DSO" are often used interchangeably. The subtle distinction: DSO calculates collection velocity on credit sales, while AR days describes the overall aging of your outstanding balances. In practice, both metrics tell the same story about whether your billing cycle is working. DSO applies differently across practice structures: Solo practices tracks whether a small team is keeping up with claims and patient follow-up Dental groups reveals consistency (or inconsistency) across multiple locations DSO organizations benchmarks centralized billing office performance across the entire portfolio A DSO under 30 days means payments arrive quickly and your revenue cycle is healthy. A DSO over 45 days means earned revenue is sitting idle in unpaid claims and overdue patient balances that should and can be in your bank account. For context on how DSO intersects with patient experience, see dental DSO benchmarks and patient experience data. How We Built These 2026 DSO Benchmarks These benchmarks draw from our analysis of dental revenue cycle data across solo practices, multi-location groups, and DSO organizations. We cross-referenced findings against published industry reports: the Zentist 2026 RCM Trends Report, Dental Economics payment goal benchmarks, and Outsource Strategies International AR reporting. Our evaluation methodology: We scored practice performance across five criteria DSO days, AR aging distribution, collection rate, denial rate, and patient balance recovery. Each score was then mapped to a practice-type profile: solo, group, or DSO. Practices in the top quartile across all five criteria achieve under 25 days DSO consistently. The benchmarks here reflect what the best-run practices actually achieve. Each tier is a realistic, attainable target for a practice willing to invest in its revenue cycle. Practices that implement the strategies in this guide should expect measurable DSO improvement within 60–90 days. Full normalization of the AR aging report typically takes 4–6 months. How to Calculate Your Practice's DSO The dental practice DSO average is calculated with a simple formula, and running it monthly gives you more revenue cycle insight than almost any other metric. The formula: DSO = (Accounts Receivable ÷ Total Credit Sales) × Number of Days Worked example: If your practice has $75,000 in outstanding AR and $90,000 in total production last month: DSO = ($75,000 ÷ $90,000) × 30 = 25 days Excellent If the same practice had $150,000 in AR, the DSO would be 50 days a clear signal of billing delays or patient balances accumulating. Two calculation methods: Rolling 30-day method: Use the prior 30 days of collections as the denominator. Best for spotting month-to-month trends quickly. Countback method: Start from the most recent month and subtract monthly gross sales from the AR balance until it reaches zero, counting the applicable days. More accurate for longer-term benchmarking. Most practice management software including OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, and CareStack can generate the AR and production figures you need automatically. Run this calculation monthly and compare it against the benchmark scorecard below. DSO Benchmarks for Dental Practices: 2026 Scorecard Use this table to locate your practice in the benchmark spectrum. Each tier reflects both DSO range and the collection rate that typically accompanies it. Revenue Cycle Performance Benchmarks Performance Tier DSO Range What It Means Collection Rate Excellent Under 25 days Top-tier performance; typical of centralized DSO billing offices with full RCM automation 98%+ Good 25–30 days High-performing group practice with standardized billing workflows 96–98% Acceptable 30–45 days Industry average; manageable but improvable; most practices land here 91–95% Poor 45–60 days Cash flow pressure; often indicates inconsistent follow-up or elevated denial rates 84–91% Critical 60+ days Significant RCM breakdown requiring immediate action; claims are aging and patient balances are escaping Below 84% Sources: Dental Economics benchmarking data ; Outsource Strategies International RCM reporting ; Dental Billing Assist KPI benchmarks What the tiers mean for your cash flow: Acceptable to Good is a realistic near-term target for most practices. The leap from 40 days to 28 days represents significant freed-up cash for a $90,000/month practice, that's roughly $36,000 no longer sitting in unpaid AR. Good to Excellent requires billing automation, consistent denial management, and clean claims submitted on the day of service. It's achievable but requires investment in process and tooling. Critical practices must treat DSO recovery as a practice-survival issue, not an optimization exercise. Immediate AR work-down of the 90+ day bucket is the first step. DSO Benchmarks by Practice Type: Solo, Group, and DSO Dental practice DSO averages differ meaningfully by practice structure because the available resources, staffing, and systems differ too. Solo Practices Typical DSO: 40–60 days Main challenges: One or two staff members managing scheduling, billing, and patient communication simultaneously. Manual claim submission, limited bandwidth for denial follow-up, and no dedicated billing role. Achievable target: 30–40 days with improved upfront insurance verification, same-day claim submission, and automated patient billing statements. The opportunity: Even a 10-day DSO improvement for a $90K/month solo practice frees $30,000 from AR real cash flow without adding staff. Group Practices (Multi-Location) Typical DSO: 30–45 days Main challenges: Inconsistent front-desk workflows across locations create variable billing quality. AR aging can look dramatically different at location A versus location B, making the aggregate DSO misleading. Achievable target: 25–35 days with centralized billing oversight, standardized workflows, and location-level AR reporting. See more on DSO call center strategy for multi-location dental groups. DSO Organizations Typical DSO: Under 25 days (top performers); 35–60 days (average, across all portfolio locations) Advantages: Centralized billing offices (CBOs), standardized denial management workflows, and RCM automation at scale give DSOs structural advantages that solo and group practices can't replicate with headcount alone. Achievable target: Under 25 days organization-wide with a functioning CBO, electronic remittance advice (ERA) posting, and consistent denial management. The gap between top-performing DSOs and average practices is primarily a workflow discipline gap, not a technology gap. Top performers run clean claims, follow up on every aging bucket, and catch denials before they pass 30 days regardless of their specific software stack. The most important DSO insight for practice operators: A well-run billing process in a centralized DSO billing office is the single most powerful driver of DSO reduction, capable of taking a portfolio from 45+ days to under 25 days without increasing headcount. AR Aging Benchmarks Beyond DSO DSO is your headline metric, but the AR aging report is the diagnostic that tells you where the breakdown is occurring. A healthy aging report for dental practices looks like this: AR Aging Bucket Targets Aging Bucket Target % of Total AR Risk if Exceeded 0–30 days 85%+ Low 31–60 days Under 10% Medium — active insurance follow-up required 61–90 days Under 5% High — patient balance escalation protocol needed 90+ days Under 3% Critical — only 15–25% of this bucket is recoverable Sources: Dental Economics payment goal benchmarks ; Pearly dental AR benchmarking The 90+ day rule is non-negotiable: Industry data consistently shows that only 15–25% of dental AR past 90 days is ever collected. Once a balance passes 120 days without resolution, recovery rates fall even further. The 90+ day bucket is the most unrecoverable segment in dental revenue cycle management the cost of ignoring it is not delayed cash, it is permanent write-off. AR ratio as a second check: Your total AR should not exceed one month's average production . A practice producing $90,000/month should carry no more than $90,000 in total AR (a 1.0x ratio). A ratio above 1.5x signals that production is outpacing collections a structural problem, not a temporary billing backlog. Key action thresholds: Any insurance claim past 30 days without a payer response → follow up immediately Any patient balance past 60 days without a payment arrangement → escalate to collections protocol Any aging bucket above target → identify the contributing payer or patient segment and address it specifically, not the AR report as a whole Clean Claims: Documentation, Compliance, and Verification High DSO is almost always downstream of upstream documentation failures. The industry standard for a clean claim requires specific documentation attached at submission and skipping any element adds days to your DSO. Clean Claim Documentation Requirements Every dental claim that is submitted without errors requires: Accurate CDT codes procedure codes must match the documented treatment and the payer's allowed code list Supporting clinical documentation X-rays, narrative descriptions, and periodontal charting for procedures that require them (extractions, implants, crowns, periodontal therapy) Pre-authorization confirmation many plans require pre-authorization for high-value procedures; submitting without it guarantees a denial Correct patient demographics date of birth, subscriber ID, and payer ID must match exactly what the payer has on file Provider credentials NPI, tax ID, and group/individual billing configuration must be correct and current A single missing field can trigger an automatic denial. The most effective prevention is real-time claim scrubbing before submission automated checking that catches missing or mismatched fields before the claim leaves the practice. Real-Time Eligibility Verification Real-time insurance eligibility verification is the highest-impact upstream intervention for reducing DSO. It confirms coverage, deductibles, frequency limitations, and benefit maximums electronically at the time of scheduling or check-in. Practices that verify eligibility before every appointment reduce eligibility-related denials by up to 60%. Best practice: verify 48–72 hours before the appointment. This allows time to correct errors before the patient arrives. Re-verify at check-in for same-day appointments. Modern systems OpenDental, Denticon, and CareStack support real-time eligibility checks through clearinghouse integrations. Compliance Considerations Dental billing systems handle protected health information (PHI) and financial data, requiring HIPAA compliance at every layer: EFT enrollment: Electronic funds transfer with major payers reduces payment turnaround by 5–10 days and eliminates virtual credit card fees that erode collections Secure patient billing: Automated billing platforms must use HIPAA-compliant encryption for patient statements and payment portals Role-based access controls: Billing staff should have access limited to the data required for their role a HIPAA requirement and an internal control that prevents errors and unauthorized changes DSO Limitations: What the Metric Doesn't Capture DSO is the best single-number summary of revenue cycle performance. But it has real limitations operators need to understand: It averages out location-level variance: A DSO of 35 days at the portfolio level can mask locations running at 18 days and others at 90 days. Location-level DSO tracking is essential for multi-site groups. It doesn't separate insurance from patient AR: High insurance AR and high patient AR require different interventions. Track them separately. It can look artificially good after write-offs: Writing off uncollectable balances improves DSO without actually improving collections. Track write-off rate alongside DSO to get the true picture. It doesn't capture production efficiency: A practice can improve DSO by reducing production more patients with faster cash cycles. Always benchmark DSO alongside collection rate and total production. What's Driving High DSO in 2026? Rising insurance denial rates, incomplete automation adoption, and front-desk staffing pressure are the three structural forces pushing dental practice DSO higher in 2026. Dental practices that managed a DSO of 35 days in 2022 may find themselves at 45–50 days in 2026 running the same processes. Three structural shifts explain why: Rising insurance denial rates. Claim denial rates in dentistry climbed from roughly 11% in 2022 to approximately 15% in 2024–2026, according to dental billing industry data . More than three-quarters of dental practices report experiencing increased claim denials or heightened payer scrutiny over the past 12 months, per the Zentist 2026 RCM Trends Report . Each denial adds days to the AR cycle and rising denial rates are the single most important external driver of DSO growth in 2026. Avoidable errors at the root. Industry reporting consistently shows that most dental claim denials are preventable typically the result of missing patient data, incorrect insurance information, or submission errors that could have been caught before the claim was ever sent. This is a billing process problem, not a payer problem. Implementing a pre-submission claim scrubbing step is the most direct way to eliminate this category of DSO inflation. Patient balance collection gaps. The average dental practice collects 70–80% of the patient-owed portion of a bill well below the 90%+ target. As insurance plans shift more cost responsibility to patients through higher deductibles and co-pays, this gap is widening. Automation adoption is still incomplete. Around 58% of dental practices committed to some form of RCM automation in 2026, per the Zentist RCM Trends Report via Dentistry Today. The remaining 42% are running manual processes that cannot keep pace with rising claim complexity and denial volume. Staffing pressure on the front desk. Front-desk turnover leaves billing tasks deprioritized and incoming patient information collected inconsistently. A missed call during a busy morning is also a billing setup failure an appointment that never got booked produces nothing for the revenue cycle to collect. How to Reduce DSO: 7 Proven Strategies These seven actions address the most common DSO drivers in dental practices. Implement them in order of leverage upstream actions first, downstream cleanup second. Verify insurance eligibility before every appointment. Confirming coverage, deductibles, co-pays, and benefit maximums 48–72 hours before the visit prevents the most common source of clean claim failures. Learn how to automate insurance verification for every scheduled patient without adding manual steps for your team. Submit clean claims on the day of service. Same-day claim submission is one of the highest-leverage billing habits available. Every day a claim sits unsubmitted is a day added to DSO. Use your PMS (OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, or CareStack) to set automated end-of-day claim exports. Follow up on every claim past 30 days. No insurance claim should sit without a payer response for more than 30 days. Set a 30-day aging trigger in your billing workflow and assign specific ownership for follow-up. Automating billing inquiry management reduces the manual burden without requiring additional staff. Build a denial management workflow. Every denial should be categorized by reason code, corrected, and resubmitted within five business days. Track denial reasons by payer patterns reveal systemic issues with how a specific carrier is being billed, not just individual errors. Send patient statements within 7 days of insurance posting. Delayed patient billing is a leading cause of patient AR aging. Automated statement delivery via email, text, or paper shortens the patient billing cycle and dramatically reduces follow-up call volume. Collect at the point of service. Practices that collect the patient-owed portion at checkout eliminate a significant slice of patient AR before it can age. For larger balances, offer payment plans with automatic recurring payments not monthly manual collection attempts. Review the AR aging report weekly, not monthly. Monthly reviews are too slow: a claim can move from 30 to 60 days in a single billing cycle. Weekly reviews catch exceptions before they become write-offs. Assign a specific team member to own the aging report and act on exceptions within 48 hours. How Front-Desk Operations Affect Your DSO Most dental practices treat DSO as a billing department problem. The biggest leverage points, however, are upstream in how calls are answered, how appointments are booked, and how patient information is collected before billing begins. Missed calls inflate DSO mathematically. Dental practices miss up to 35% of inbound calls, according to call handling industry data . Each missed call can be a missed appointment and an appointment that never gets booked produces nothing. When total production decreases, DSO increases even if billing is running perfectly, because the denominator in the DSO formula (total credit sales) shrinks. Recapturing missed production directly improves your DSO calculation. Collecting insurance data on the scheduling call eliminates downstream errors. When patients call to book, capturing their insurance carrier, member ID, and date of birth at that moment lets your team verify eligibility 48 hours before the appointment rather than scrambling at check-in or discovering errors after the claim is submitted. Eligibility failures at check-in are a leading source of claim denials. Front-desk accuracy determines billing accuracy. If patient information is entered incorrectly during scheduling a wrong date of birth, a transposed subscriber ID that error flows into the claim. A denial 30 days later adds another 2–4 weeks to your DSO. Getting it right on the first call is the most cost-effective denial prevention available. Arini's AI receptionist for dental practices handles inbound calls 24/7, books directly into your PMS (OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, CareStack, and more), and collects insurance information during the scheduling call giving your billing team clean, verified data from the very first patient interaction. At Unified Dental Care, this approach contributed to a 12% revenue increase. At Kare Mobile , Arini captured $56K in new patient appointments in the first month. Accurate upstream data is the foundation of a clean billing cycle. Learn how an AI receptionist reduces front-desk overhead without adding headcount. Key Features for DSO Protection 24/7 call answering in 300ms every inbound call answered, zero missed production Insurance data collection on the scheduling call carrier, member ID, and date of birth captured before the appointment Direct PMS integration books appointments into OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, CareStack, and more HIPAA compliant encryption and role-based access controls across the platform After-hours and overflow coverage no calls fall through during lunch, peak hours, or evenings Natural-sounding conversations patients interact naturally without knowing they're speaking with an AI; the experience is indistinguishable from a trained front-desk team member Best For: Solo practices and dental groups that miss calls during peak hours, have front-desk staff stretched across billing and scheduling, or want to eliminate upstream billing errors without adding headcount. Pricing: Demo-based contact Arini for practice-specific rates. Book a Demo see how an AI receptionist that answers calls in 300ms, collects insurance data on every call, and books directly into your PMS can protect your revenue cycle before billing even begins. The Financial Impact of DSO Improvement The dollar value of DSO improvement is larger than most practice operators realize and it compounds at the portfolio level. For a solo practice producing $90,000/month: Moving from 50 days DSO to 30 days frees roughly $60,000 from AR (20-day improvement × $3,000/day) That's cash that was already earned but sitting idle in unpaid claims and patient balances For a multi-location group producing $500,000/month: A 15-day DSO reduction releases approximately $250,000 from AR At a 5x EBITDA multiple common in dental acquisitions, that improvement translates to $1.25M in enterprise value For a DSO organization with $50M annual revenue: Moving the collection rate within 30 days from 71% to 78% generates approximately $3.5M in additional annual collections At a 5x valuation multiple, that improvement translates to roughly $17.5M in additional enterprise value driven purely by revenue cycle discipline These figures are consistent with benchmarks from dental RCM analytics providers tracking large DSO portfolios. DSO improvement is not an administrative project. It is one of the highest-return financial investments a dental organization can make. How Long Does It Take to See Results? Starting from a DSO of 50+ days, the path to 30 days or below is achievable but it takes sustained effort across several months. Here's a realistic timeline based on industry experience: Weeks 1–4: Baseline and quick wins Run your first DSO calculation and full AR aging report Identify the top 10 overdue insurance claims by dollar value and follow up immediately Implement 30-day aging triggers for insurance claims going forward Set up automated patient statements within 7 days of insurance posting Weeks 5–12: Process standardization Launch insurance pre-verification 48–72 hours before appointments for all scheduled patients Establish same-day claim submission as a mandatory daily close-out task Assign denial management ownership with a 5-business-day rework window Move to weekly AR aging reviews; track bucket percentages against benchmarks Months 4–6: Systematic improvement visible Practices implementing these changes consistently see measurable DSO reductions within 90 days Collection rates should improve noticeably as the 31–60 day and 61–90 day buckets shrink The 90+ day bucket should begin declining as you stop adding new balances to it Practices in critical territory (60+ days) should treat the 90+ day AR bucket as the immediate priority contacting every balance over $500, offering payment arrangements, and writing off irrecoverable balances that are distorting the overall metric. Learn how to recover aged AR across insurance and patient balances to free up billing bandwidth during the recovery period. Frequently Asked Questions What is a good DSO for a dental practice? A DSO under 30 days is considered good for a dental practice. Under 25 days is excellent and typical of top-performing DSO organizations with centralized billing and full RCM automation. The 30–45 day range reflects the industry average acceptable but improvable. Anything above 45 days signals cash flow pressure and a billing cycle that needs attention. What is the average AR days for dental practices? The dental practice DSO average sits in the 30–45 day range for practices with standard billing processes. Solo practices often run higher 40–60 days due to limited billing bandwidth and manual processes. Multi-location groups with standardized workflows typically achieve 30–45 days, and DSO organizations with centralized billing offices can reach under 25 days. How do I calculate DSO for my dental practice? Divide your total accounts receivable by your total credit sales (production), then multiply by the number of days in the period. For monthly tracking: DSO = (AR ÷ Monthly Production) × 30. A practice with $75,000 in AR and $90,000 in monthly production has a DSO of 25 days an excellent result. What % of AR Should Be Over 90 Days in Dentistry? Top-performing dental practices keep AR over 90 days below 3% of total AR. An acceptable ceiling is 10%. Anything above that is a significant problem industry data shows that only 15–25% of dental AR past 90 days is typically recovered. Once balances age past 120 days, recovery rates fall even further. What causes high days sales outstanding in dental billing? The most common causes include: delayed claim submission, insurance denials that go unchallenged past 30 days, missing or incorrect patient insurance data causing clean claim failures, slow patient statement delivery, and insufficient bandwidth to work the aging AR report consistently. Rising insurance denial rates now approximately 15% industry-wide in 2026 have made denial management more important than it was just a few years ago. AR Days vs. DSO: What's the Difference in Dentistry? AR days and DSO are closely related but different measures. DSO calculates how quickly a practice collects payment on credit sales using the formula (AR ÷ Credit Sales) × Days. AR days, or days in AR, refers to the aging of the overall AR balance how long outstanding balances have been sitting without collection. In practice, most dental billing teams use the terms interchangeably, and both metrics point to the same underlying revenue cycle performance. How does Arini's AI receptionist help reduce DSO? Arini addresses DSO from the upstream before the billing cycle begins. By answering every inbound call 24/7 and collecting insurance information during the scheduling call, Arini ensures your billing team has accurate patient and insurance data from day one. Missed calls reduce total production (shrinking the denominator in the DSO formula), which mathematically inflates DSO even when billing is working correctly. Arini's 24/7 coverage means every call gets answered, every appointment gets booked, and the billing cycle starts with clean information. See how improving missed call percentage directly impacts revenue cycle performance. How can I improve my practice's DSO quickly? Three high-impact starting points include: (1) immediately following up on every claim past 30 days that has no payer response, (2) implementing 48-hour insurance pre-verification for all scheduled patients, and (3) sending patient statements within 7 days of insurance posting. These three actions can show measurable DSO improvement within 30–60 days. For longer-term gains, reducing front-desk overhead with AI automation frees your billing team to focus on AR management rather than call routing. What Happens When You Ignore High DSO Too Long? AR past 90 days has only a 15–25% recovery rate and that window narrows further past 120 days. A practice that lets DSO stay above 60 days for six or more months is quietly writing off a growing portion of earned revenue each month, often without noticing until the impact shows up as cash flow pressure or a need for a credit line. Sustained high DSO also distorts practice valuation for prospective buyers. Addressing it requires a full AR work-down of the 90+ day bucket, correction of the underlying process failures, and several months of consistent execution to normalize the aging report. Is 30 days DSO good for a dental practice? Yes, 30 days DSO is considered good for a dental practice. The industry benchmark places 25–30 days in the "good" tier above the industry average of 30–45 days. Under 25 days is excellent and typical of centralized DSO billing offices with full RCM automation. Most solo practices run 40–60 days DSO, making 30 days a meaningful and achievable improvement target for practices willing to invest in their billing process. How long does it take to improve DSO in a dental practice? Most dental practices see measurable DSO improvement within 30–60 days of implementing upstream changes like 48-hour insurance pre-verification and same-day claim submission. Moving from 50+ days DSO to under 30 days typically takes 4–6 months of consistent execution across all revenue cycle steps. Practices in critical territory (60+ days) should prioritize an immediate AR work-down of the 90+ day bucket before focusing on systemic process improvements. What is a healthy AR ratio for a dental practice? A healthy AR ratio for a dental practice is 1.0x or lower meaning total accounts receivable should not exceed one month's average production. A practice producing $90,000 per month should carry no more than $90,000 in total AR. An AR ratio above 1.5x signals that production is outpacing collections and requires immediate intervention to prevent permanent write-offs in the 90+ day aging bucket. Where to Start If Your DSO Is Above 45 Days A DSO above 45 days means cash flow is tighter than it needs to be and AR is actively aging into unrecoverable territory. Here's where to focus: This week: Run your aging report. Identify every claim past 30 days without a payer response and follow up on the largest balances first. This month: Implement 48-hour insurance pre-verification before appointments and same-day claim submission as a daily close-out standard. This quarter: Build a denial management workflow and shift to weekly AR aging reviews. Track your DSO monthly to measure progress. Ongoing: Protect the upstream every missed call and every scheduling error is a downstream billing problem waiting to happen. title: Your Quick Guide to the 2021 Open Enrollment Period
body_text: Categories Health Insurance / Healthcare / Medicare / Obamacare FAQ Your Quick Guide to the 2021 Open Enrollment Period By HealthSherpa Share this post Once a year, all eligible Americans get a chance to shop the Health Insurance Marketplace and get a Marketplace plan, also known as Obamacare or an Affordable Care Act plan. This time is known as the annual Open Enrollment Period (OEP). The Affordable Care Act (ACA) ensures that all eligible Americans get this opportunity once a year to buy affordable health coverage for themselves and their families. And the ACA also means that all plans available on the Marketplace offer the following key consumer protections: For 2021, the Open Enrollment Period runs from Sunday, November 1 through Tuesday, December 15, 2020 in most states. Coverage purchased during the OEP window will begin on January 1, 2021 You can shop available plans and compare prices here or enter your zip code below to see available plans. Who is eligible to shop during Open Enrollment? Not sure if you’re eligible to shop the Marketplace for an Obamacare plan? Good news: Most people are! If you are a U.S. citizen, national or legal resident of the United States who currently resides in the U.S., you’re qualified to shop the Marketplace. This includes green card holders, refugees, asylees, and individuals with non-immigrant status who have a valid worker visa. The only exceptions? If you’re currently enrolled in Medicare or currently incarcerated. Grab our free step-by-step guide to enrolling in Marketplace coverage to learn more. Keep in mind that if you are offered ACA-compliant health insurance by your employer and choose to opt-out of it and instead purchase your own Obamacare plan, you usually won’t be eligible for any subsidies and will need to pay full price for your monthly premiums. Because of this, if you have access to health insurance coverage through your employer, we recommend you utilize that instead of the Marketplace, unless your employer insurance costs more than 9.61% of your household income. For everyone else, though, welcome to shopping the Marketplace during OEP! We’ve tried to compile all the essential information you’ll need to make this year’s OEP as seamless as possible for you. Remember that should you have any questions at all, the HealthSherpa Consumer Advocate Team is here to help and can be reached at 872-228-2549. You can shop available plans and compare plan premiums here . Enrolling on HealthSherpa only takes an average of 15 minutes. During Open Enrollment Period, anyone who’s eligible can enroll in a Marketplace health plan. The rest of the year is known as Special Enrollment Period (SEP), and you’ll need a Qualifying Life Event (QLE) such as losing your health coverage, having a child, getting married, or another change in household size or health coverage. When can I shop the Marketplace during Open Enrollment? In most states, Open Enrollment Period runs from November 1st, 2020 to December 15, 2020. Some states, however, have extended their Open Enrollment Period. This means that anyone living in these states will have extra time to enroll. Regardless of which state you live in, you can shop for a 2021 plan at any point during Open Enrollment. So far for the 2021 OEP, the following states have extended Open Enrollment Periods to the following dates: Minnesota: Dec 22, 2020 Colorado: Jan 15, 2021 Nevada: Jan 15, 2021 Pennsylvania: Jan 15, 2021 Washington: Jan 15, 2021 Massachusetts: Jan 23, 2021 Rhode Island: Jan 23, 2021 California: Jan 31, 2021 District of Columbia: Jan 31, 2021 New Jersey: Jan 31, 2021 New York: Jan 31, 2021 We will update this list as any other states announce extended Open Enrollment Periods. Will I have to pay a fine if I don’t have health insurance in 2021? Congress repealed the penalty for having health insurance in 2018. That means in most states, you won’t have to pay a fine if you go without coverage in 2021. However, California, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Rhode Island, and DC have passed their own individual mandates. This means you may have to pay a penalty to the state if you go without coverage for a certain period of time. No matter which state you live in, it’s important to remember that health insurance limits your financial risk. All Marketplace plans have an annual out of pocket maximum, which means that if you receive high medical bills, you’ll only pay a portion of the cost. After I enroll during Open Enrollment Period, when does my health insurance begin? Almost everyone who enrolls during Open Enrollment Period (OEP) will have insurance coverage beginning on January 1, 2021. This coverage will continue until Dec. 31, 2021 as long as all monthly premium payments are made. If you gain other coverage during this period—for example, through a new job—you can cancel your Marketplace plan at any time. Did you enroll for Obamacare in a state with an extended OEP? Then your coverage may have a different start date. Check with your local state exchange for more details about your start date if you enroll during the extended enrollment period. What do I need when I’m ready to enroll? You’ll need some basic information on-hand to get started with the Open Enrollment process. First, you’ll need to provide information about your household, including household size (including anyone you claim on your tax return). For each of these people, you’ll need some basic information like birth dates, home addresses, and social security numbers. Additionally, you’ll need information about your best estimate for your 2021 income, information on how you file your taxes if you have a spouse, information about your sources of income, and policy numbers from any current health insurance plans. A note on immigration status Although you’re providing information about every member of your tax household, you do not have to provide immigration status unless you yourself are applying for coverage. If you don’t have a social security number, you also do not need to provide this on your Marketplace application. It’s important to know that information about immigration status collected by the Marketplace is carefully protected and cannot be used for immigration enforcement. More generally, by law the personal information that you provide on this form can only be used to determine your eligibility for coverage and to enroll you in a plan, and must be stored securely. If anyone in your household is a Permanent Resident, you’ll need their Resident Alien (A-number) ready. Typically, you will just need to enter the number, but you may need to upload the document so have it ready to scan in case you need it. You can find out about what documents you will need for other eligible immigration statuses here . What if I already have a plan from last year? If you had Marketplace health insurance in 2020, you will be automatically re-enrolled in that plan for next year if that plan is still being offered. If that plan is no longer available, you’ll be enrolled in an “equivalent” plan. Although that might sound like the easiest way to approach OEP, it isn’t necessarily your best option. In fact, people who who shop and switch plans save an average of 38% on their monthly premiums. Most insurers are expanding their coverage areas this year, which means there will be more plans available to you. Without shopping to compare what plans, and savings, are available to you this year, your premium payments may increase substantially. Plan details can change from year to year, too, meaning that prescription coverage, provider networks, and coverage benefits could change even if you keep the same plan. By shopping the Marketplace, you’ll find out what kinds of available plans might best suit your needs for the coming year, and what cost savings you will be eligible for with those plans. It only takes a few minutes to shop and compare your options, and this can keep you from paying more later. What about subsidies, cost-sharing reductions, and tax credits? Many Americans are eligible to save on their health insurance costs as a result of the Affordable Care Act. No matter where you live, if you earn between 100 – 400% of the Federal Poverty Level (determined by the federal government) and aren’t eligible for Medicaid , you will qualify for a premium tax credit that will help lower your premium costs. By 2020’s FPL numbers , this meant that a family of four whose combined household income was between $26,200 and $104,800 would qualify for a premium tax credit. Depending on your income, you may also qualify for Cost Sharing Reductions (CSR), which are special savings built-in to Silver-level Marketplace plans for people who earn between 100 and 250% of the federal poverty limit. These CSRs limit and reduce out-of-pocket costs like copays and deductibles. Remember that if you are married and do not file taxes jointly with your spouse, you will not be eligible for any subsidies or CSRs in the Marketplace. How do I sign-up for Marketplace insurance during Open Enrollment? Want to enroll in Marketplace insurance for 2021 but not sure where to start? We have a step-by-step breakdown of how to shop the Marketplace and what that process looks like here . In short, you can self-enroll online , have a Consumer Advocate help you over the phone, find local, in-person assistance , or complete and mail-in a paper application. Applying online through HealthSherpa, a certified enrollment partner of the government, is straightforward and simple. If you’re unfamiliar with HealthSherpa, know that we offer all of the same plans at the exact same prices as HealthCare.gov, the government’s enrollment site. The difference? We offer a simpler enrollment process, a website that’s easier to use, and have a phenomenal Consumer Advocate team on-hand to help you at each step along the way. Reachable by phone, email, and online chat, our Consumer Advocate Team are here to help both before and after you sign up for your new Obamacare plan. Our advocates are licensed health insurance experts with a background in advocacy, not salespeople. It only takes an average of around 15 minutes to complete an application on HealthSherpa, versus an average of 56 minutes when using Healthcare.gov . Of course if you have any questions before Open Enrollment begins or would like assistance in choosing a plan, please feel free to call our Consumer Advocate Team anytime at (872) 228-2549 . We’re here to help you navigate the Open Enrollment Period process and find the best possible plan for your needs. You can see plans and prices, and see how much financial help you’re eligible for, by entering your zip below. What about other coverage options like Medicare and Medicaid? You can apply for Medicaid year-round here—there’s no need to wait for an Open Enrollment Period. You can apply for Medicaid here . If you’d like to enroll in Medicare, you’ll become eligible three months before your 65th birthday, and you may become eligible earlier if you have certain disabilities. You can learn more about Medicare here . If you’re already enrolled in a Medicare plan and you’d like to make changes to it, Medicare open enrollment runs from October 15 to December 7. During this annual enrollment period (AEP), you can make changes to your coverage, such as switch between Original Medicare and a Medicare Advantage plan, or vice versa. If you have any questions, give our Consumer Advocate Team a call at (872) 228-2549 .

With more clarity upstream, Solution Designers pass blueprints to Solution Builders, Pega’s developer and architect community working in Pega Infinity Studio™ , a new intuitive app development environment announced today at PegaWorld that combines AI speed with enterprise class reliability and governance. Organizations can move beyond AI experimentation to sustainable transformation, improving speed and quality while closing the gap between business ambition and working software. A sustained investment in people – not just technology This initiative outlines a clear vision for enterprise transformation – where AI amplifies, not replaces, human capabilities – reflected in its three pillars: Free, progressive credentials via Pega Academy : A skills‑based credentialing model validates proficiency in Pega Blueprint AI, the methodology, and the capabilities needed to guide AI‑driven transformation, replacing role‑based certifications with a framework aligned to project needs and clearer paths for practitioners and organizations. Blueprint Delivery workshop series: In‑person workshops go beyond technical training to build core capabilities, from facilitation and stakeholder alignment to outcome‑driven execution. Organizations can request onsite workshops to bring needed Blueprint Delivery skills directly to their teams. A thriving global community: The rapidly growing Pega Blueprint AI and App Design Expert Circle and its thousands of members provide an ongoing network of practitioners sharing knowledge, patterns, and expertise through peer conversations, blogs, videos, and webinars. Reimaging how business works with AI Pega Blueprint AI is transforming how enterprise software is designed and delivered, making rapid ideation, real-time collaboration, and AI-powered design core to every engagement. As it evolves, so will the delivery model. Early Blueprint Delivered adopters show AI delivers the most value when paired with human judgment. Pega’s end to end Blueprint Delivered methodology turns AI powered designs into production ready applications with proven results for clients including 50% faster discovery and ideation, 80% of projects going live in 90 days or less, and 30% less rework after initial design. Availability: Solution Designer enablement will be available for free in Pega Academy with the upcoming launch of Pega Infinity™ 26. The Pega Solution Designer Initiative will be highlighted today on the main stage at PegaWorld , Pega’s annual user conference, held at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. For more information, visit www.pega.com/solution-designer . title: These Boots Are Made For Walking
summary: A fitness influencer says walk more to burn more. An evolutionary anthropologist says that math is wrong. Drs. Boz and Sauvé explain what's actually happening — and why it matters for your brain.
body_text: If you want to start an argument among psychiatrists, ask a simple question: ‍ What fuel does the brain actually run on? ‍ Glucose? Ketones? Both? ‍ One thing is clear: the brain is an energy-intensive organ, consuming roughly 20% of the body’s metabolic budget. When energy metabolism becomes unstable, mood, cognition, and emotional regulation suffer. ‍ Which brings us to a surprisingly powerful metabolic intervention: walking after meals. ‍ A fitness influencer recently blessed my feed with “three hacks to make fat loss faster through walking.” His advice: get your steps up, take walks after meals, and when that stops working, crank up the incline on your treadmill. ‍ He’s not wrong, exactly. He’s just not interesting. ‍ The framing is pure calories-in-calories-out: walk more, burn more, lose fat. It’s the metabolic equivalent of explaining that cars move because the wheels turn. Technically accurate. Utterly missing the point. ‍ Let me tell you what’s actually happening when you take a walk after dinner—and why it matters far more than the 47 calories your Apple Watch says you burned. ‍ The Hadza Paradox Herman Pontzer is an evolutionary anthropologist at Duke who had a reasonable hypothesis: hunter-gatherers who walk 10-14 kilometers per day must burn dramatically more calories than sedentary Westerners. ‍ He was wrong. ‍ Using doubly labeled water—the gold standard for measuring energy expenditure—Pontzer found that Hadza hunter-gatherers in Tanzania burn approximately the same number of calories per day as American office workers. Hadza men: ~2,600 kcal/day. Hadza women: ~1,900 kcal/day. Statistically indistinguishable from adults in the U.S. or Europe after controlling for body size. ‍ Let that sink in. People who spend their lives scratching a living out of the earth with hand-made tools—who move more in a morning than most Americans move in a week—burn the same energy as their sedentary Western counterparts. ‍ Pontzer’s “Constrained Energy Expenditure” model explains why: total energy expenditure increases with physical activity at low levels, then plateaus . The body adapts. It down-regulates other metabolic processes to keep total expenditure within a narrow, evolutionarily-conserved range. ‍ Frankly, this stretches my understanding of physics. We’re talking about 10-14 kilometers of daily walking—somewhere in the neighborhood of 15,000-20,000 steps. What processes could possibly be down-regulated enough to account for that difference? The implication is remarkable: the range in which the human body can burn fuel to accomplish the same work is extraordinarily broad. And when there’s excess energy coming in, the body even knows how to waste it—mitochondrial uncoupling proteins can essentially disconnect the turbines and just produce heat, burning fuel without generating ATP. ‍ We’re not simple calorimeters. We’re adaptive metabolic systems with millions of years of evolutionary pressure to maintain energy homeostasis. The body has more tricks than your fitness tracker knows about. ‍ So when our fitness influencer says “push harder on the incline to burn more calories”—he’s fighting millions of years of metabolic conservation. The body will find a way to compensate. It always does. ‍ Exercise prevents you from getting sick. Diet is your tool for weight management. These are Pontzer’s words, not mine. ‍ But here’s where it gets interesting: if walking isn’t primarily about burning calories, why does it work so well for metabolic health? ‍ It’s the Glucose, Not the Calories When you eat, blood glucose rises. This is true no matter what you eat—even if you consume zero carbohydrates. The very act of eating protein induces an insulin response, which in turn triggers compensatory glycogen release and even gluconeogenesis. Your body is determined to maintain glucose homeostasis, and it will manufacture glucose from protein if it has to. Eating is a metabolic event, period. ‍ Insulin rises in response, signaling cells to take up that glucose. In a metabolically healthy person, this happens efficiently—glucose clears, insulin drops, and you return to a state where lipolysis (fat breakdown) can occur. ‍ In someone with insulin resistance, this process is sluggish. Glucose stays elevated longer. Insulin stays elevated longer. And as long as insulin is elevated, lipolysis is suppressed. You’re locked out of your own fat stores. ‍ Here’s what a post-meal walk actually does: It bypasses insulin entirely. ‍ Muscle contraction activates GLUT4 transporters through an insulin-independent pathway mediated by AMPK. You’re literally pulling glucose out of circulation without requiring an insulin spike to do it. This isn’t just “using fuel”—it’s a fundamentally different metabolic route. ‍ A 10-minute walk immediately after eating reduces peak blood glucose significantly—from ~182 mg/dL to ~164 mg/dL in one study. That blunted glucose excursion means a blunted insulin response. And a blunted insulin response means you return to a lipolytic state faster. ‍ The calories burned during that walk? Trivial. ‍ The reduction in insulin exposure? That’s the game. ‍ The Math Your Treadmill Won’t Tell You Speaking of calories: those readouts on exercise equipment are, to use the correct meaning of the word, gross estimates. Not “ew, gross”—gross as in rough, approximate, unrefined. ‍ If you think you can walk on a treadmill until the display reads “500” and conclude you’ve burned a seventh of a pound of fat, you’re relying on tragically flawed math. The actual number depends on your body composition, metabolic rate, fitness level, what you ate, your hormonal state, and roughly a dozen other variables the machine knows nothing about. ‍ But more importantly: even if the number were accurate, it wouldn’t matter much. Because the Hadza taught us that energy expenditure is constrained. You can’t out-walk your metabolism’s determination to conserve energy. ‍ This brings me to something that frustrates me about the way people talk about wanting to make their bodies more “efficient.” ‍ In most aspects of life, efficiency is the opposite of what you want. ‍ You don’t want your body to be a Prius—relatively weak power output with maximized fuel storage and minimal use. That’s a body optimized for scarcity, hoarding every calorie against an uncertain future. ‍ What you actually want is a supercharged V-8: maximum power output, minimal storage, burning fuel freely because there’s plenty more where that came from. A body that builds muscle instead of fat. A metabolism that runs hot. ‍ And this will happen if you “tell” your body the right things. (Remember: listening to your body works, as long as you learn the language.) ‍ If your body understands that fuel availability is practically infinite—that famine is not coming—and that the number one thing needed for survival is power output , it will do what any self-respecting engineer would do: build you a muscle car. ‍ When insulin is low, the fat spigot is wide open, and you’re feeding the machine with plenty of high-quality protein and fat, that is exactly the message you’re sending. You’re signaling abundance and demand. The body responds by building capacity, not storage. ‍ What you can do is change the metabolic environment. And that’s where the post-meal walk earns its keep—not by burning calories, but by bending the glucose and insulin curves. ‍ The Snowball Effect (Or: Why Consistency Beats Intensity) Here’s the part nobody talks about. ‍ When you walk after a meal and successfully blunt your glucose/insulin response, you create a window for lipolysis. Fat gets mobilized. Ketones get produced. And your mitochondria—the power plants in every cell—get exposed to a different fuel mix. ‍ Mitochondria are adaptive. They upregulate the enzymatic machinery for whatever substrate is abundant. Feed them glucose all day, every day, and they’ll optimize for glucose oxidation. Expose them regularly to fatty acids and ketones, and they’ll build the infrastructure to burn fat preferentially. ‍ Here’s the kicker: mitochondria turn over every 4-6 weeks. You’re not stuck with the metabolic machinery you have today. You’re building new mitochondria constantly—and they’re being shaped by the metabolic environment you create. ‍ So imagine you walk after meals consistently. Each walk: ‍ Pulls glucose down via insulin-independent GLUT4 translocation Blunts the insulin response Opens a window for lipolysis Exposes mitochondria to elevated fatty acids and ketones ‍ Do this regularly, and you’re voting—with every walk—for what kind of metabolism you want next month. ‍ Over time: ‍ More fat/ketone exposure → mitochondria that prefer fat oxidation Fat-adapted mitochondria → less glucose demand → lower baseline insulin Lower insulin → less insulin resistance → even easier access to fat stores Easier lipolysis → more ketone exposure → next generation of mitochondria even more fat-adapted ‍ This is metabolic compounding. The first walk is the hardest. The 100th walk is running on different hardware. ‍ The Caveat: Hyperinsulinemia Changes the Rules Now, a dose of reality for those of us who aren’t metabolically pristine. If you’re significantly insulin resistant, you likely have chronic hyperinsulinemia—elevated baseline insulin that doesn’t drop easily. In this state, you can walk for hours and primarily just deplete glycogen. Insulin stays high because it can’t drop (or won’t, because your pancreas is overcompensating for resistant tissues). Without that insulin drop, you never fully access lipolysis. You’re draining the battery without switching to the generator. ‍ This isn’t futile—glycogen depletion is still useful, and the GLUT4/AMPK pathway still works. But you won’t get the clean switch to fat oxidation that a metabolically flexible person gets. ‍ There is a phenomenon—sometimes called “the flip”—where prolonged exercise eventually forces the issue. Deplete enough glycogen, get hypoglycemic enough that your body has no choice, and insulin will finally fall. Ketones will finally rise. But we’re talking hours, not minutes. ‍ I experienced this firsthand on a 20-mile hike in Colorado a few years back. At the time, I was in a moderately insulin-resistant phase—fasting glucose running 90-100 mg/dL, ketones minimal at 0.5-0.7 mmol/L. For most of that hike, I felt suboptimal. Running on sugar and glycogen, never quite clicking into a higher gear. ‍ But at mile 20, I checked my blood. Ketones: over 4.0 mmol/L. ‍ That was the flip. Hours of glycogen depletion finally forced insulin down, and my liver started producing ketones at a rate I’d never seen. I’d essentially walked my way into therapeutic ketosis—the hard way. ‍ The lesson: if you’re insulin resistant, the post-meal walk still helps. It’s still bending the curves in the right direction. But the full metabolic cascade takes longer to unlock. Patience and consistency matter more than intensity. ‍ Metabolic Psychiatry (Or: Why This Matters Beyond the Mirror) Here’s where my day job as a psychiatrist intersects with metabolic physiology. ‍ Glucose variability—the spikes and crashes that come from poor metabolic control—doesn’t just affect your waistline. It affects your brain. Mood, cognition, energy, emotional stability: all of these are downstream of metabolic function. ‍ The brain is an energy hog. It’s roughly 2% of your body weight but consumes about 20% of your metabolic budget. And while the old dogma held that the brain runs exclusively on glucose, we now know it runs beautifully on ketones—arguably better on ketones, which provide more ATP per unit oxygen consumed than glucose does. ‍ When you’re metabolically flexible—when you can access fat and produce ketones readily—your brain has a steady, high-quality fuel source. When you’re locked into glucose dependency with wild swings in blood sugar, your brain is along for the ride. Every spike and crash registers. The afternoon slump. The brain fog. The irritability that comes out of nowhere. The anxiety that spikes two hours after a high-carb meal. ‍ This isn’t just “feeling off.” Chronic glucose variability drives inflammation. And inflammation in the periphery becomes neuroinflammation in the brain. The same metabolic dysfunction that promotes insulin resistance also promotes the inflammatory signaling that underlies depression, anxiety, and cognitive decline. ‍ But here’s the flip side: ketones aren’t just fuel. Beta-hydroxybutyrate—the primary ketone body—is a signaling molecule. It inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation, one of the key drivers of inflammatory cascades. It’s essentially an endogenous anti-inflammatory that you produce for free every time you access your fat stores. ‍ So when you take that post-meal walk and successfully blunt your glucose response, open a window for lipolysis, and produce some ketones, you’re not just managing your weight. You’re: ‍ Reducing glucose variability → more stable mood and cognition Lowering systemic inflammation → less neuroinflammation Producing beta-hydroxybutyrate → active anti-inflammatory signaling Providing your brain with premium fuel → clearer thinking, more sustained energy ‍ The subjective experience of this is hard to overstate. You don’t just feel “better”—you feel steady . The emotional rollercoaster flattens out. The energy peaks and troughs smooth into something more like a plateau. You stop white-knuckling your way through the afternoon. ‍ Mental health is physical health. The artificial separation between the two has always been a failure of imagination. Your brain is an organ. It runs on metabolism. Fix the metabolism, and the brain comes along for the ride. ‍ The Punchline The fitness influencer wants you to think about walking as a calorie furnace. Stoke it hotter, burn more fuel, lose more fat. ‍ The metabolic reality is different. Walking—especially post-meal walking—is a glucose disposal intervention. An insulin-management strategy. A mitochondrial training program. ‍ The boots aren’t made for burning calories. ‍ They’re made for building mitochondria. ‍ Walk today, and you’re not just handling this meal’s glucose. You’re casting a vote for what kind of metabolism you want next month. And the month after that. ‍ That’s not a hack. That’s a compounding investment in your metabolic future. ‍ Nancy Sinatra knew what she was talking about. ‍ This article was originally published on Dr. Boz's Substack
